lines: Mind the loom. Threads tangle faster when people crowd them.
Give the loom room. Woolwork works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the loom. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the loom, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Mind the wool baskets. They shed onto everyone equally.
Hello. If you left a gate open, tell me before I guess.
You caught me between counting and counting again.
Step lightly. The flock is suspicious of sudden importance.
Good timing. The loom is behaving for once.
Come closer, but do not startle the lambs.
I can talk while the wool settles.
Welcome. Try not to stand where the sheep want to be.
The day is calm, which means I am checking the fences twice.
Speak up. The flock has been answering questions nobody asked.
Hello there. Leave the dye pots to those with fewer regrets.
I was sorting wool by color and mood. Mostly color.
Stand by the post and tell me what you need.
Good to see you without a trail of escaped sheep.
You have my attention until someone bleats like a crisis.
